sections.heading: AcmeDB 2.0 migration guide
sections.text: Upgrade every driver to 1.8 or newer. 2.0 drops the v1 wire protocol. Rename to in . 2.0 refuses to start on the old key. Restart the server on 2.0. Run and fix anything it flags. Take a first snapshot with . From 1.7 or older, dump and reload instead of upgrading in place.

sections.heading: AcmeDB docs — architecture
sections.text: URL: https://example.com/acmedb/docs#architecture Kind: documentation Reliability: high Give-a-shit: medium Accessed: 2026-10-24, demo-freeze day

sections.heading: What it says
sections.text: Every write is appended to the write-ahead log and fsynced before it is acknowledged. A single manifest file records the live set of sorted tables. AcmeDB does not shard. One node owns the whole keyspace.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The durability story is simple enough to audit: WAL, fsync, manifest. The same page rules out horizontal scale; there is no partitioning layer to tune.

sections.heading: Used for
sections.text: AcmeDB acknowledges only durable writes AcmeDB shards the keyspace across nodes

sections.heading: AcmeDB docs — backups
sections.text: URL: https://example.com/acmedb/docs#backups Kind: documentation Reliability: high Give-a-shit: high Accessed: 2026-10-24, demo-freeze day

sections.heading: What it says
sections.text: Point-in-time snapshots are coming soon. Cross-region replication is on the roadmap. The page documents one operation: a manual dump to a local file. There is no scheduled backup, no managed snapshot, and no restore-to-timestamp.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: This is the vendor's own reference documentation, so a gap here is a gap in the product. Anyone running AcmeDB today owns their own backups.

sections.heading: Used for
sections.text: AcmeDB has no managed backups AcmeDB is single-region only

sections.heading: AcmeDB issue #412 — cross-region replication
sections.text: URL: https://example.com/acmedb/issues/412 Kind: issue tracker Reliability: medium Give-a-shit: high Accessed: 2026-10-24, demo-freeze day

sections.heading: What it says
sections.text: Multi-region is not planned for this year. Run one region and ship your dumps somewhere else. The issue has 140 upvotes and one maintainer reply. It is still open.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It turns the docs' "on the roadmap" into a date: not this year.

sections.heading: Used for
sections.text: AcmeDB is single-region only

sections.heading: AcmeDB launch post
sections.text: URL: https://example.com/acmedb/launch Kind: self-published Reliability: medium Give-a-shit: low Accessed: 2026-10-24, demo-freeze day

sections.heading: What it says
sections.text: p99 read latency under 2ms on a laptop. AcmeDB is a durable key-value store. No consensus, no sharding, no surprises. The post links no benchmark harness, names no dataset size, and reports no write latency.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is marketing. The latency number is the vendor's best case on one machine, and nobody has reproduced it.

sections.heading: Used for
sections.text: AcmeDB serves p99 reads under 2ms

sections.text: AcmeDB has no managed backup and no point-in-time restore today.

sections.heading: Claim
sections.text: An acknowledged write survives a crash: AcmeDB fsyncs each write to its write-ahead log before acknowledging it.

sections.heading: Verdict

documents.title: AcmeDB shards the keyspace across nodes

sections.heading: AcmeDB shards the keyspace across nodes
Claim
sections.text: AcmeDB partitions its keyspace across several nodes for horizontal scale.

sections.heading: Verdict
sections.text: Refuted. The architecture page says one node owns the whole keyspace.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: AcmeDB docs — architecture: "AcmeDB does not shard. One node owns the whole keyspace."

sections.heading: Claim
sections.text: AcmeDB serves p99 point reads in under 2 milliseconds.

sections.heading: Verdict
sections.text: Unverified. The only evidence is the vendor's own benchmark, run on a laptop, with no published harness. Treat 2ms as the ceiling, not the floor.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: AcmeDB launch post: "p99 read latency under 2ms on a laptop."

sections.heading: Claim
sections.text: AcmeDB runs in a single region. There is no cross-region replication.

sections.heading: Verdict
sections.text: Supported. The docs put replication on the roadmap, and the maintainers say it is not planned this year.

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.text: AcmeDB docs — backups: "Cross-region replication is on the roadmap." AcmeDB issue #412 — cross-region replication: "Multi-region is not planned for this year."

sections.heading: AcmeDB research desk
sections.text: This is the research pack behind the knap verdicts on AcmeDB. Every source a verdict cites has a page here, and every claim is pinned to the source it came from.
